title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #3

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these words is a noun? (1 mark)
   A. millet
   B. slowly
   C. tasty
   D. boil

2. A noun is a word that (1 mark)
   A. describes a colour only
   B. shows an action
   C. names a person, animal, place or thing
   D. joins two sentences

3. Which action shows attentive listening? (1 mark)
   A. Looking out of the window
   B. Drawing on your desk
   C. Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   D. Talking to a friend

4. A verb is (1 mark)
   A. a word that shows an action
   B. a word that names a person
   C. a joining word
   D. a word that describes a colour

5. Fluent reading needs (1 mark)
   A. only a quiet voice
   B. only loudness
   C. only speed
   D. smooth pace, correct words and good expression

6. What is the first thing to do when someone gets a burn? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Cover it with dirt
   C. Put the burn under cool running water
   D. Rub it hard

7. What should you do if you did not hear a question? (1 mark)
   A. Politely ask for it to be repeated
   B. Leave
   C. Guess loudly
   D. Laugh

8. Which question word asks for a reason? (1 mark)
   A. When
   B. Who
   C. Where
   D. Why

9. What is the best way to read your part in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Read it very quickly
   B. Read other people's lines
   C. Practise your lines with the right feeling
   D. Never practise

10. What is the main idea of a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. What the paragraph is mostly about
   B. The last word
   C. The number of lines
   D. The title font

11. In The farmer was weary after a long day in the shamba, weary means (1 mark)
   A. very tired
   B. very loud
   C. very rich
   D. very hungry

12. Which is a good way to check a proverb's meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an elder or teacher
   B. Ignore it
   C. Guess forever
   D. Cover it

13. What is the setting of a story? (1 mark)
   A. Where and when it happens
   B. The last line
   C. The price
   D. The name of the writer

14. Which is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. It is Monday
   B. A stitch in time saves nine
   C. Please sit down
   D. Bring your book

15. Which strategy would you use to find a price in an advert? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing
   B. Skimming
   C. Singing
   D. Scanning

16. What is a conman? (1 mark)
   A. A person who tricks people to get money
   B. A teacher
   C. A farmer
   D. A shopkeeper

17. What should you check when you reorder jumbled words? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the letters
   B. Nothing
   C. That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   D. The paper

18. What is a receipt? (1 mark)
   A. A paper that shows you paid
   B. A shop
   C. A type of fruit
   D. A kind of coin

19. What are the two main parts of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Title and ending
   B. Noun and verb only
   C. Capital and full stop
   D. Subject and predicate

20. Which is a poem's mood if it is joyful? (1 mark)
   A. Sad
   B. Happy
   C. Sleepy
   D. Angry

21. Which question helps you find ideas from a picture? (1 mark)
   A. Who is in the picture?
   B. How heavy is the paper?
   C. Who printed it?
   D. What page is this?

22. Why should a writer plan a story before writing? (1 mark)
   A. To lose the ideas
   B. To avoid a title
   C. To organise the ideas
   D. To skip the ending

23. Which is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. It repeats the title
   B. It has no meaning
   C. It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   D. It begins a new topic

24. What is community service? (1 mark)
   A. Sleeping
   B. Selling goods
   C. Helping the community without pay
   D. Playing only

25. Which feeling does Ouch! show? (1 mark)
   A. Disgust
   B. Pain
   C. Sleepiness
   D. Joy

26. What should you do in a reading competition? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Whisper
   C. Read very fast
   D. Read clearly with the right intonation

27. Which punctuation mark often follows an interjection showing strong feeling? (1 mark)
   A. Full stop
   B. Exclamation mark
   C. Colon
   D. Question mark

28. How should notes be written? (1 mark)
   A. As long sentences
   B. As short phrases of key words
   C. As whole paragraphs
   D. As drawings only

29. What is a stage direction? (1 mark)
   A. A price
   B. The ending
   C. The title
   D. An instruction to the actor placed in brackets

30. What should you do first when a call is answered? (1 mark)
   A. Greet politely
   B. Hang up
   C. Ask for money
   D. Shout

31. Which adjective describes colour? (1 mark)
   A. large
   B. tall
   C. silver
   D. thin

32. What can you use to make a poster advert? (1 mark)
   A. A blank page
   B. Only a number
   C. A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   D. Only a full stop

33. What does interpret mean? (1 mark)
   A. To sell it
   B. To hide it
   C. To explain what something means
   D. To tear it

34. Why should you write true information on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody reads forms
   B. Forms are records and false information causes problems
   C. False answers are best
   D. It is a game

35. Why should you ask an adult before giving your address on an online form? (1 mark)
   A. No reason
   B. To stay safe
   C. To make it longer
   D. To waste time

36. What is a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. A solo song
   B. A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   C. A quiz
   D. A game of football

37. What does a class monitor do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives
   B. Runs the school
   C. Helps lead the class
   D. Cooks

38. Which is a polite way to interrupt? (1 mark)
   A. You are wrong!
   B. Excuse me, may I say something?
   C. Be quiet!
   D. Stop talking!

39. What is the message of a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The main idea the poet wants to share
   B. The number of lines
   C. The printer
   D. The date

40. What are non-verbal cues in a performance? (1 mark)
   A. Written words
   B. Music only
   C. Gestures and facial expressions
   D. Loud shouting

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

42. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

43. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

44. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

45. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)

46. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

47. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

48. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

49. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

50. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)

51. Give two rules for looking after class library books. (2 marks)

52. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)

53. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

54. Read: Millet porridge is a warm drink made by mixing millet flour with water and boiling it. What is it made from and how is it cooked? (3 marks)

55. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

56. Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper. (3 marks)

57. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

58. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — millet
   Millet is a grain, so it names a thing. The others are an action, a describing word and an adverb.

2. C — names a person, animal, place or thing
   Nouns are naming words.

3. C — Looking at the speaker and staying quiet
   Attentive listening means giving your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker.

4. A — a word that shows an action
   Verbs show what is done.

5. D — smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   These are the parts of fluency.

6. C — Put the burn under cool running water
   Cool water reduces pain and damage.

7. A — Politely ask for it to be repeated
   Asking politely helps you answer correctly.

8. D — Why
   Why asks the reason.

9. C — Practise your lines with the right feeling
   Practice with expression helps fluency.

10. A — What the paragraph is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

11. A — very tired
   A long day of work suggests tiredness.

12. A — Ask an elder or teacher
   Elders can explain the meaning.

13. A — Where and when it happens
   Setting means place and time.

14. B — A stitch in time saves nine
   It is a short saying that gives advice.

15. D — Scanning
   You know exactly what you need.

16. A — A person who tricks people to get money
   A conman deceives others.

17. C — That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   A sentence must make sense.

18. A — A paper that shows you paid
   A receipt is proof of payment.

19. D — Subject and predicate
   Every sentence has a subject and a predicate.

20. B — Happy
   A joyful poem has a happy mood.

21. A — Who is in the picture?
   Who, where, what and why give story ideas.

22. C — To organise the ideas
   A plan gives the story shape.

23. C — It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

24. C — Helping the community without pay
   Community service benefits others.

25. B — Pain
   People say ouch when hurt.

26. D — Read clearly with the right intonation
   Clear reading with expression is judged.

27. B — Exclamation mark
   Exclamation marks show strong feeling.

28. B — As short phrases of key words
   Notes are brief.

29. D — An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   Stage directions tell how to speak or move.

30. A — Greet politely
   A greeting begins the call.

31. C — silver
   Silver is a colour.

32. C — A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   Adverts have these parts.

33. C — To explain what something means
   To interpret is to explain meaning.

34. B — Forms are records and false information causes problems
   Honest answers are important.

35. B — To stay safe
   Personal details should be protected.

36. B — A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   A panel discusses a topic.

37. C — Helps lead the class
   A monitor helps the teacher lead.

38. B — Excuse me, may I say something?
   It asks permission politely.

39. A — The main idea the poet wants to share
   The message is the main idea.

40. C — Gestures and facial expressions
   Non-verbal cues are actions without words.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Turn pages gently, never write in them, return them on time, keep them clean (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is made from millet flour and water and it is cooked by boiling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for millet flour, one for water, one for boiling.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule, up to three.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
